caseno: Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 231 of 2010
lawyer:
Goutam Kumar Roy, Deputy Attorney General instructed by Md. Shamsul Alam, Advocate-on-Record ----- For the Petitioners 
N.K. Saha, Senior Advocate instructed by Zainul Abedin, Advocate-on-Record ----- For the Respondent
parties:
Government of Bangladesh represented by the Secretary Dhaka and others ----- Petitioners
Vs.
Bimal Saha alias Jhantu Saha and other ----- Respondents
full_judgment: 3. The case of the writ-petitioners is that they are the sons of Mohan Saha of village-Birulia, under Police Station- Savar, District- Dhaka. During preparation of the record-of-rights under the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950, the landed property measuring an area 9.59 acres of Mouza Shamiar, under Police Station-Savar, District- Dhaka was recorded in S.A. Khatian No. 15 and S.A. Plot No. 67 (hereinafter referred to as the landed property) in equal share in the names of Gopi Ballav Saha and Nan Ballav Saha. The landed property appertained to C.S. Khatian No. 4. Thereafter the landed property was recorded in R.S. Plot Nos. 176 and 177 in R.S. Khatian No. 55 of Mouza Shamair in the name of said Gopi Ballav Saha in equal share. Gopi Ballav Saha died leaving behind the writ-petitioners as two sons who inherited the entire 9.59 acres of the landed property. The writ-petitioners by a registered power of attorney dated the 31st day of January, 2004 appointed Alhaj Md. Abdul Hai, son of late Haji Amir Chan Bepari of No. 24 Katasur, Police Station- Mohammadpur, District-Dhaka as their attorney in order to do all acts in civil, criminal and revenue Courts as well as in all other statutory bodies for protection and well management of the landed property. The attorney of the writ-petitioners applied to writ-respondent No. 3, the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue), Dhaka for mutation of their names in the relevant record-of-rights. On the said application; writ-respondent No. 4, the Assistant Commissioner (Land), Savar Upazila by Memo No. জেঃ প্রঃ ঢাঃ/ বাঃ বিবিধ সা-২/২০০৩-৭৪০ (নং) dated the 10th day of May, 2004 called for a report through writ-respondent No. 5, the Kanongo and accordingly, the Kanongo submitted a report on the 12th day of July, 2004 stating that S.A. recorded tenant - Gopi Ballav Saha had left the country during India-Pakistan war and as a result, 4.80 acres of land of S.A. Khatian No. 15 in his share was recorded as vested property in V.P. Case No. 338/75, the said 4.80 acres of land was leased out to Akub Ali, Suruj Ali, Joynal Abedin and Kuri Fakir. The said 4.80 acres of land has been enlisted at serial No. 966 under Vested Property Return Act, 2000. During the R.S. operation, S.A. Plot No. 67 was split up in two R.S. Plots being Nos. 176 and 177 covering 9.31 acres and .28 acre respectively and the same were recorded in R.S. Khatian No. 55 in he names of Gopi Ballav Saha and Pran Ballav Saha. During the R.S. operation, the landed property was not recorded as vested property. On the 13th day of July, 2004, writ-respondent No. 4 transmitted the report to writ-respondent No. 3 for necessary action. Despite receiving the aforesaid report of the Kanongo, writ-respondent No. 4 did not pass any order in the matter and hence the writ-petitioners filed V.P. Appeal No. 215/2004 before writ-respondent No. 6, the Additional Divisional Commissioner, Dhaka who by his order dated the 31st day of July, 2004 declared the entire proceedings including the order passed in V.P. Lease Case Nos. 235 of 76 and 338/75 illegal and void and directed writ-respondent No.4 to allow the proposed mutation subject to approval of writ-respondent No.1, the Government of Bangladesh, represented by the Secretary, Ministry of Land and he sent the record of V.P. Appeal No. 215 of 2004 to writ-respondent No. 1 for approval. Thereafter, writ-respondent No. 1 on perusing the aforesaid order and the documents on record vide Memo No. ভূঃ মঃ/ শঃ-৬/অর্পিত/ঢাকা/১৫২/২০০৪/৩৮৮ dated the 19th day of May, 2005 asked writ-respondent No. 2, the Deputy Commissioner, Dhaka to inform whether action was taken pursuant to the order of the Additional Divisional Commissioner or the aggrieved party filed any appeal against the same. Having noticed the reluctance of writ-respondent Nos. 2, 3 and 4 in taking necessary action for the proposed mutation, the writ-petitioners filed Miscellaneous Appeal No. 351/2006 before writ-respondent No. 7, the Chairman, Land Appeal Board, Dhaka stating all the aforesaid facts upon which he passed an order on the 13th day of July, 2006 directing writ-respondent Nos. 2, 3 and 4 to take necessary action in the light of the letter dated the 19th day of May, 2005 of writ respondent No. 1 Even after receiving the aforesaid order of writ-respondent No. 7, writ-respondent Nos. 2, 3 and 4 kept silent and reluctant as before. In the circumstances, the writ-petitioners again filed an application before writ-respondent No. 6, the Additional Divisional Commissioner; Dhaka in V.P. Appeal No. 215/2004 for compliance with the order passed by the Land Appeal Board, the Secretary Ministry of Land as well as the order dated the 31st day of July, 2004 passed by him. In the said V.P. Appeal No. 215 of 2004, writ-respondent No. 6 by his order dated the 15th day of February, 2007, directed writ-respondent No. 4, the Assistant Commissioner (Land) for mutation of the names of the writ-petitioners in the record-of-rights.
